messages:
Alex: Quick follow-up on the shallow-resume idea from the RFC — I sketched an early handoff that only preserves a small prefix fingerprint and per-stream offsets rather than full K/V snapshots. Thought we should call out the tradeoffs.
Mira: Nice. Can you sketch the handshake flow? how do we avoid replayed tokens or dup outputs?
Alex: Short version: upstream produces a ResumeToken after an N-token stable prefix. Downstream can request resume with that token. Token contains prefix_hash, seq_offset, and a small opaque epoch id.
Devon: So we rely on prefix_hash for semantic equality, not full KVC? That's lighter but brittle for models that expand context (e.g., streaming system prompts)
Alex: Right. That's the trade: low memory and cheap metadata vs strict correctness for side-effectful requests. We mitigate with conservative windows and server-side dedupe for idempotent endpoints.
Raj: What about server memory / KV cache? With shallow resume we don't reconstruct the full KV cache; we replay into a fresh KV up to seq_offset?
Alex: Exactly. We replay only the missing tail. The resume token gives you the offset to continue from; the edge will fetch the last M tokens from durable prefix store for local warmup.
Sylvie: If we replay tokens we still need to be careful about costs and latency. Replaying 1k tokens could blow latency SLOs.
Mira: Can we combine shallow resume with progressive KV warmup? i.e., resume fast with low-quality short context, then background-warm KV for long context and update user stream with no-op patches if generated tokens change?
Devon: Patches are messy for callers. But could be OK if we surface a resumable flag: fast-resume vs strict-resume.
Alex: Proposed modes:
- fast-shallow: resume with prefix_hash+offset, minimal replay, best-effort determinism (default for non-side-effect endpoints)
- strict-reconstruct: full KV restore + deterministic replay, guaranteed identical outputs (opt-in, higher cost)
Mira: How do we express this in the API? route config? per-tenant policy?
Raj: Route-level annotation seems right. Also fallback to strict if we detect high-risk prompts (webhook side-effects). We can detect via evals or heuristics.
Sylvie: Observability: we need token-level metrics: resume_mode, replay_tokens, resume_success, divergence_detected. Prefer per-request tags.
Alex: Agreed. infra-bot, can you add a telemetry ticket template?
infra-bot: Created infra ticket #INF-4721: "Resume telemetry: resume_mode, replay_tokens, resume_latency, divergence_rate" (link: https://tracker/internal/INF-4721)
Devon: Edge-level memory bound: reserve N MB per active shallow-resume stream for replay buffer. If exceeded, drop to fast-no-replay and annotate "degenerate".
Mira: And add circuit-breaker: if divergence_rate > 0.1% for a route over 1h, auto-escalate to strict-reconstruct.
Alex: Good. One more: resumable token format suggestion:
```
ResumeToken {
  bytes prefix_hash;   // blake2b-64
  uint32 seq_offset;   // token index of stable prefix
  uint32 epoch;        // monotonic generation id for upstream
  string route_id;     // route fingerprint for compatibility
}
```
Raj: Need HMAC sign for tamper-proofing if tokens flow client-side.
Alex: Yes — sign with route-specific key and short TTL (minutes). We don't allow indefinite tokens.
Sylvie: Action items:
- Alex: draft thin API annotation for resume_mode and token format (PR)
- Mira: short eval harness to measure divergence frequency across common prompts
- Devon: memory/circuit-breaker proposal for edge runtime
- Raj: KMS/HMAC design note for token signing
- infra-bot: ticket INF-4721 created
Alex: Let's aim to sync next Wed and decide defaults for hosted vs dedicated tiers.
Mira: Sounds good. thanks.
Devon: Thanks — leaning toward fast-shallow default for user-facing chat, strict for webhooks.
Alex: End of thread.
